newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares inch higher in quiet Christmas trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares inch higher in quiet Christmas trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices edged higher on Wednesday in quiet Christmas trading which was still monopolised by popular housing firm Heliopolis Housing and Development, brokers said.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index inched 0.27 points higher to 286.2 points on average volume of 41.72 million pounds ($12.3 million). Volume on Tuesday was a heavy 81.05 million pounds ($23.84 million).
"There's nothing dramatic going on because of the holiday season. The foreign investors are a big part of the market," said Khaled Mahmoud of El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
Heliopolis Housing continued to top trade for the second day running. The firm, the day's most active, accounted for almost 11 million pounds of turnover but fell 12 pounds to 418.

Broker Youssef Khalil of Delta/EAB said blue-chip Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was selling some of its shares in Heliopolis Housing through the bourse while others said rumours that the firm would give shareholders a free share for every two shares had stirred up trade.
"It's a strong company and perhaps the only exception in the bourse where most sectors are sleepy," Khalil said. "Things will definitely look up in about two weeks."
Investors continued to buy Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN shares ahead of the government's proposed sale of some of the firm through a global depository receipt offering in January.
Share ended one pound down at 126 in turnover of 3.74 million pounds.

Brokers said both the milling and cement sectors, mainstays of the bourse, were mostly stable but some shares tended upwards. Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose 3.21 pounds to 64.2 and Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA rose 0.25 to 63.5.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 431.42 points from 429.28 on Tuesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 201.01 from 201.29.
Of the 75 shares traded, gainers outnumbered losing stocks 33 to 17 while the rest ended unchanged.
